LESSON: READING 3.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: ETIQUETTE - TELEPHONE Suggested Vocabulary phone, telephone, mobile, dial, cell 
Topic 3.2: Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading, part of ETIQUETTE - TELEPHONE Suggested Vocabulary phone, telephone, mobile, dial, cell  in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do you obtain information from a text? 2. Why do you need to infer the meaning of unfamiliar words?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  in purposive groups, skim and scan a text for specific information,  in purposive groups, read a text of up to 500 words on etiquette,  Answer direct and inferential questions,  Use contextual clues such as : synonyms and antonyms as well as neighbouring words to infer the meaning of fixed phrases, similes, metaphors, idioms, proverbs and phrasal verbs,  Use a dictionary to check the meaning of unfamiliar words. . Learners who may not perform the practical task could point/ carry out the task orally while being offered physical support.  In purposive groups, Collaborate to Create a crossword puzzle using 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1.  in purposive groups, skim and scan a text for specific information,  in purposive groups, read a text of up to 500 words on etiquette,  Answer direct and inferential questions,  Use contextual clues such as : synonyms and antonyms as well as neighbouring words to infer the meaning of fixed phrases, similes, metaphors, idioms, proverbs and phrasal verbs,  Use a dictionary to check the meaning of unfamiliar words. . Learners who may not perform the practical task could point/ carry out the task orally while being offered physical support.  In purposive groups, Collaborate to Create a crossword puzzle using 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Learning to Learn: The learner’s ability to learn on their own is encouraged as they complete tasks and infer the meaning

of words using contextual clues.

 Creativity and Imagination: – The learner’s artistic prowess is enriched as they generate ideas when creating a crossword

puzzle using vocabulary from the text read.

Values:
Unity: Cooperation is cultivated as the learner displays team spirit while creating a crossword puzzle using vocabulary from the

text read.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion: The learner acquires the skills of living harmoniously with others by reading texts on etiquette.

Link to other Subjects
